  "title": "Spectral Cross-Modal Guidance: Training-Free Selective Amplification of World Knowledge for Robust Action Generation",
  "core_problem": "World-Action Models (WAMs) achieve near-saturated performance on standard manipulation benchmarks (Being-H0.7: 99.2%, Fast-WAM: 97.6% on LIBERO) but remain brittle under geometric perturbations — camera viewpoint and robot initial state changes cause drops to 60–90% on LIBERO-Plus. Concurrently, Fast-WAM, GigaWorld-Policy, and MotuBrain demonstrate that video features are dispensable at inference under standard conditions. These facts appear contradictory: if video-encoded spatial knowledge is dispensable, why do WAMs fail precisely under geometric perturbations where spatial reasoning should matter most? We hypothesize the resolution lies in HOW video information is used, not WHETHER it is used. Under standard conditions, the action branch encodes sufficient visual-motor mappings from the training distribution, making video features redundant. Under geometric perturbation, these mappings break — and the video branch's spatial reasoning could compensate, but only if the video→action guidance signal is properly amplified and filtered. Standard classifier-free guidance (CFG) in diffusion models amplifies all conditional contributions equally, mixing action-relevant spatial information with irrelevant appearance features. CPC theory (NeurIPS 2025) proves CFG implicitly performs selective amplification via contrastive principal components, but only in class-conditional settings with well-separated covariance structures — not in heterogeneous cross-modal settings like video→action guidance. The core question: can explicit spectral filtering of the cross-modal guidance signal selectively amplify geometric/spatial components that improve robustness while suppressing components that add noise? Before answering this, a prior diagnostic question must be settled: does cross-modal guidance in WAMs carry any action-relevant signal at all under geometric perturbation? No existing work has tested this.",
  "opportunity": "Three converging developments create a precise research opportunity, and a critical correction from the prior proposal version enables a more principled approach: (1) UWM (RSS 2025) uses UniDiffuser-style independent diffusion timesteps for video and action modalities — setting the video timestep t_o'=T marginalizes video information, yielding the unconditional action score, while t_o'<T yields the video-conditioned action score. This natively enables cross-modal CFG through two forward passes without any dropout training, architectural modification, or fine-tuning. UWM releases a pretrained LIBERO-90 checkpoint. (2) LIBERO-Plus and the WAM robustness study (March 2026) reveal that geometric perturbations remain the dominant failure mode: OA-WAM Geo-Avg 84.3% (Camera 80.5%, Robot 89.6%), CKT-WAM (Camera 77.4%, Robot 71.4%), with the overall LIBERO-Plus SOTA at 86.1% (CKT-WAM). Crucially, all geometric robustness improvements to date (OA-WAM, CKT-WAM) require architectural modification or additional training — no training-free inference-time method has been attempted. (3) Independent Condition Guidance (ICG, ICLR 2025) demonstrates that CFG-quality guidance can be obtained from any pretrained conditional model without dropout training, by substituting the unconditional score with a prediction conditioned on a random/independent input. This enables cross-modal guidance on WAMs like Fast-WAM that were not trained with video dropout. (4) DiffStateGrad (ICLR 2025) establishes SVD-based subspace projection for filtering diffusion guidance signals, but only in single-modal image restoration. CRITICAL CORRECTION: The prior version incorrectly claimed Fast-WAM was trained with unconditional video feature dropout enabling native CFG. After verification — reading the full paper, project page, and GitHub — this claim is unsupported. Fast-WAM uses CFG scale 1.0 (no guidance amplification), and 'uncond' in checkpoint names refers to its unconditional inference mode (no future video denoising), not CFG-enabling dropout training. UWM's independent timestep mechanism provides the principled alternative, with ICG as a backbone-agnostic complement.",
  "landscape": "**Video-at-inference in WAMs:** Fast-WAM (March 2026) removes video denoising at inference, retaining only backbone features. GigaWorld-Policy (March 2026) uses causal masking to block video→action flow. MotuBrain (April 2026) freezes video branch and caches KV pairs. All use binary approaches (all or no video features) and evaluate only on standard benchmarks — none test under geometric perturbation. **Cross-modal CFG support in WAMs:** UWM (RSS 2025) uses independent diffusion timesteps for video and action, enabling native cross-modal conditioning control by setting t_o'=T to marginalize video. Motus (Dec 2025) uses a similar UniDiffuser-style architecture. X-WAM (April 2026) uses asynchronous noise sampling across modalities. Vid2World (ICLR 2026) applies CFG in the action→video direction for video quality. DreamZero (Feb 2026) uses parallelized CFG for real-time inference. No work systematically applies or evaluates cross-modal CFG in the video→action direction for action quality or robustness improvement under perturbation. **Training-free guidance methods:** ICG (ICLR 2025) provides CFG-quality guidance on any pretrained conditional model using independent/random conditions, without dropout training — validated on image generation but not cross-modal robot control. **CFG Theory:** CPC decomposition (NeurIPS 2025) proves CFG implicitly decomposes into mean-shift + positive CPC + negative CPC; explicitly notes limitations when conditional covariances lack discriminative structure — the expected case for heterogeneous video→action conditioning. **SVD-based guidance filtering:** DiffStateGrad (ICLR 2025) projects measurement gradients onto SVD subspaces for image restoration. Related SVD approaches exist for controllable editing (Feb 2025) and concept removal (March 2025). All operate in single-modal image settings; none address cross-modal guidance for robot control. **Geometric robustness methods (competitors):** OA-WAM (May 2026): object-addressable architecture, Geo-Avg 84.3% (Camera 80.5%, Robot 89.6%) — requires architectural modification. CKT-WAM (May 2026): parameter-efficient context transfer, total 86.1% (Camera 77.4%, Robot 71.4%) — requires additional training. Being-H0.7 (May 2026): latent world-action queries with posterior alignment, 82.1% zero-shot / 84.8% fine-tuned — uses implicit world modeling without explicit video branch. π0.5: 85.7% total. AnyCamVLA (March 2026): zero-shot camera adaptation via feed-forward novel view synthesis, training-free but VLA-specific and camera-only. ADPro (2025): test-time adaptive diffusion policy via manifold-constrained denoising, evaluated on RLBench/CALVIN but not LIBERO-Plus. GPC (Feb 2025): inference-time enhancement via predictive world model look-ahead, requires a separately trained world model. **Selective world-model usage:** WoG (Feb 2026) compresses world predictions via learned Q-Former — requires retraining. FFDC (May 2026) decides WHEN to replan, not HOW MUCH or WHICH influence to apply within denoising. **Gap:** No existing work (1) applies cross-modal CFG in the video→action direction of WAMs with systematic evaluation under geometric perturbation, (2) uses spectral filtering to selectively amplify action-relevant components of the cross-modal guidance signal, or (3) provides a training-free, architecture-agnostic method targeting WAM geometric robustness specifically.",
  "approach": "We propose Spectral Cross-Modal Guidance (SCG), a training-free inference-time method for selectively amplifying action-relevant world knowledge in WAMs, targeting geometric robustness. The approach is structured in two phases: a diagnostic phase establishing whether cross-modal guidance carries useful signal under perturbation, and a method phase applying spectral filtering if signal exists.\n\n**Phase 1 — Cross-Modal Guidance Diagnostics (primary empirical contribution).** Before spectral filtering, we answer the foundational question: does amplifying video→action guidance improve WAM robustness under geometric perturbation? Using UWM's independent timestep mechanism, we compute the guidance vector g_t = ε(a; t_a, t_o'=t_a) − ε(a; t_a, t_o'=T) at each action denoising step t. The first term uses joint denoising (video and action at matched noise levels, exchanging information through shared attention); the second marginalizes video by setting t_o'=T (pure noise). The guided prediction: ε_guided = ε_marginal + w·g_t. We sweep w ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0} on both standard LIBERO (sanity check — expect no benefit, confirming video dispensability under standard conditions) and LIBERO-Plus geometric perturbations (camera, robot-init at L1/L3 difficulty). This takes ~25-30h H100 and definitively answers whether guidance carries signal. If uniform CFG shows zero improvement under geometric perturbation at all scales, the paper pivots to a diagnostic/negative-result contribution analyzing what video branches encode vs. what geometric robustness requires.\n\n**Phase 2 — Spectral Filtering with Action Quality Correlation (method contribution, contingent on Phase 1).** If Phase 1 reveals that uniform CFG helps (or helps inconsistently — improving some perturbation types but hurting others), we apply spectral filtering to selectively amplify beneficial components. Collect guidance vectors {g_t} across a calibration set (~100 trajectories from LIBERO training data) at each of K=10 denoising steps. For each step t, compute the SVD of the guidance covariance C_t = (1/N)Σ g_t g_t^T = U_t Λ_t U_t^T. For automatic component selection, compute Action Quality Correlation (AQC) for each principal direction u_i: the Spearman rank correlation between |u_i^T g_t| and action quality improvement (loss reduction) when the component is included. Retain components with AQC exceeding a permutation-null threshold (p<0.05), yielding projection Π_t. Filtered guidance: ε_guided = ε_marginal + w(t)·Π_t(g_t), where w(t) follows β-CFG timestep-adaptive scheduling. This extends DiffStateGrad's subspace projection from single-modal image restoration to cross-modal robot control, with the key difference being AQC-calibrated selection rather than state-defined projection.\n\n**Backbone Strategy.** Primary: UWM with released LIBERO-90 checkpoint, fine-tuned on LIBERO tasks. UWM's independent timesteps provide mathematically clean cross-modal CFG: t_o'=T gives the unconditional (video-marginalized) action score natively, with no dropout training or architectural modification needed. Secondary (extension for backbone-agnosticism): ICG applied to Fast-WAM. ICG approximates the unconditional score by conditioning on a random/independent input — for video features, this means substituting real video tokens with random embeddings sampled from a matched distribution. ICG has been validated on image diffusion models (ICLR 2025) but not cross-modal robot control; testing it here is itself a novel contribution. If ICG on Fast-WAM produces consistent results with UWM's native CFG, this demonstrates SCG's architecture-agnosticism.\n\n**Evaluation strategy.** Primary benchmark: LIBERO-Plus with 3 perturbation types — camera and robot-init (geometric, where video knowledge should help most), plus light as control (where WAMs already excel, expect no benefit from guidance). 2 difficulty levels (L1, L3), 2 seeds. Standard LIBERO as sanity check. Baselines: (i) UWM standard policy (t_o'=T, no guidance), (ii) UWM joint denoising (t_o'=t_a, no guidance amplification — equivalent to CFG w=1.0), (iii) Uniform cross-modal CFG (w>1), (iv) SCG with AQC spectral filtering (ours). Ablations: (a) AQC threshold sensitivity, (b) per-step vs. global SVD, (c) cross-task transfer of calibrated subspace (calibrate on LIBERO tasks A, evaluate on tasks B), (d) AQC-selected directions vs. top-variance directions (testing whether action-relevant ≠ high-variance), (e) ICG on Fast-WAM vs. UWM native CFG (backbone comparison). Framing vs. OA-WAM: SCG is training-free and architecture-agnostic, complementary to OA-WAM's architectural approach. We explicitly frame SCG as applicable to any WAM with video/action branches, including potentially OA-WAM itself if its checkpoint becomes available.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 5)
Issues: ["UWM BASE MODEL WEAKNESS (CRITICAL): UWM achieves only ~79% average success on standard LIBERO evaluation tasks, far below SOTA (Fast-WAM 97.6%, Being-H0.7 99.2%, MotuBrain ~95%+). Running SCG on top of a 79% baseline means even if guidance provides a 5-10% improvement under perturbation, the absolute numbers will be uncompetitive with OA-WAM (84.3% geo-avg) which starts from a stronger base. CoRL reviewers will question why the base model is so much weaker than contemporaries. The proposal must either (a) demonstrate that UWM fine-tuned on specific LIBERO tasks achieves competitive performance (the 79% is from pretraining; task-specific fine-tuning should be much higher), or (b) switch to a stronger backbone.", "UWM HAS NO LIBERO-PLUS BASELINE (HIGH RISK): UWM has never been evaluated on LIBERO-Plus. Establishing UWM's LIBERO-Plus baseline requires engineering effort (environment setup, perturbation pipeline integration) and the results are completely unknown. If UWM scores <50% on geometric perturbations (plausible given its weaker standard LIBERO performance), improvements from SCG may still leave it far below OA-WAM/CKT-WAM. This unknown should be resolved in the first 2-3 days before committing to the full plan.", "CONTINGENT METHOD CONTRIBUTION MISMATCHES USER REQUIREMENT: The user explicitly requires 'METHOD ONLY — new inference algorithm.' Phase 1 is diagnostic, not a method contribution. If Phase 1 shows no signal (high probability given Fast-WAM/GigaWorld-Policy/MotuBrain all finding video dispensable), the paper reduces to a negative empirical finding. The proposal's fallback ('significant negative result that redirects the field') does not satisfy the METHOD ONLY constraint. The proposal should have a concrete method fallback that works regardless of Phase 1 outcome.", "NULL RESULT PROBABILITY REMAINS STRUCTURALLY HIGH: Three independent lines of evidence (Fast-WAM, GigaWorld-Policy, MotuBrain) converge on video features being dispensable at inference. The hypothesis that geometric perturbation changes this is reasonable but entirely speculative — zero prior evidence supports it. The probability of Phase 1 yielding a null result (video guidance provides no benefit even under perturbation) is non-trivial, perhaps 40-60%. The proposal handles this gracefully with the two-phase structure, but doesn't adequately address what happens next.", "CALIBRATION TRANSFERABILITY REMAINS UNADDRESSED: AQC requires ~100 calibration trajectories per task to compute the SVD and select components. The proposal mentions cross-task transfer as an ablation but doesn't address whether the action-relevant subspace is stable across (a) different LIBERO tasks, (b) different perturbation types (camera vs. robot-init), or (c) different difficulty levels. If recalibration is needed per task × perturbation type, SCG's practical advantage over training-based methods (OA-WAM, CKT-WAM) is significantly reduced.", "FIELD TRAJECTORY CONCERN: Being-H0.7 (May 2026) achieves 99.2% on LIBERO and 82.1%/84.8% on LIBERO-Plus using latent world-action queries WITHOUT explicit video branches. This suggests the field is moving toward implicit world modeling where the video→action guidance signal SCG filters simply doesn't exist. SCG is architecturally specific to WAMs with explicit video branches — a shrinking target."]
Feedback: The proposal has improved substantially from Round 4 — the Fast-WAM correction, switch to UWM, and AQC contribution are genuine advances. The research question is well-framed. However, three structural issues must be resolved:

**1. FIX THE UWM BASELINE GAP (MOST URGENT):** UWM's ~79% on LIBERO is a pretraining-only number. The proposal must explicitly state (and ideally verify) that task-specific fine-tuning from the LIBERO-90 checkpoint achieves competitive performance (>90%). The UWM paper reports fine-tuning for 10K steps per task — run this first on 2-3 LIBERO tasks and report the fine-tuned success rate before committing to the full plan. If fine-tuned UWM achieves >92% on standard LIBERO, the baseline is acceptable. If it stays at ~79%, switch backbone or abandon this approach.

**2. ADD A PHASE-1-INDEPENDENT METHOD CONTRIBUTION:** The user needs a METHOD paper. Consider restructuring: instead of making Phase 2 contingent on Phase 1, propose SCG as a general framework for modality-selective guidance in multi-modal diffusion models, with UWM/WAM as the primary testbed. Even if uniform CFG shows marginal benefit, spectral filtering may still improve the guidance-quality-per-compute tradeoff (fewer effective guidance dimensions → faster convergence → fewer denoising steps). Frame the spectral compression angle as a secondary method contribution: SCG can identify which k of d guidance dimensions matter, enabling 'sparse guidance' that runs faster. This gives a method contribution (efficient selective guidance) independent of whether guidance improves robustness.

**3. ADDRESS UWM-ON-LIBERO-PLUS EARLY:** Before any SCG work, run UWM (fine-tuned) on LIBERO-Plus camera and robot-init perturbations at L1. This takes ~5-10h H100 and answers whether UWM is even competitive enough to serve as a meaningful testbed. If UWM fine-tuned achieves <60% on geometric perturbations, there's enough room for SCG to show improvement. If it achieves >80%, the room for improvement is small but any improvement would be impressive.

**4. STRENGTHEN NOVELTY ARGUMENT AGAINST CPC THEORY:** The CPC paper proves CFG implicitly amplifies 'positive CPCs' and suppresses 'negative CPCs.' Your counter-argument (heterogeneous video→action conditioning lacks well-separated covariance structures) is reasonable but hand-wavy. Sharpen it: (a) CPC analysis assumes class-conditional distributions with shared covariance structure — video→action conditioning has fundamentally different conditional and unconditional covariances because they represent different modalities, not different classes within one modality. (b) AQC selects components based on action-quality correlation, not variance — this is orthogonal to CPC's variance-based implicit selection and should capture different components. Make this argument explicitly in the paper.

**5. SCOPE ICG-ON-FAST-WAM AS EXTENSION, NOT CORE:** ICG on Fast-WAM is interesting but adds complexity and hasn't been validated for cross-modal robot control. Keep it as a single-paragraph extension experiment, not a core contribution. Focus the paper tightly on UWM + spectral filtering.

## Instructions
- Think in two phases: FIRST reconsider the problem framing (core_problem / opportunity / landscape) if the reviewer flagged issues there, THEN revise the method (approach / resource_estimate / key_references). Do not jump straight to fixing the method if the underlying problem framing needs correction.
- Address each issue specifically.

## 深度调研要求（每一轮修订都必须执行）

不要简单地'打补丁'——每一轮修订都是重新审视和深化这个 idea 的机会。

1. **深度搜索**：针对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，建议用 2-3 种不同的搜索查询调研。
   - 搜索最新的相关论文（arXiv, conference proceedings）
   - 搜索 benchmark/leaderboard 确认当前 SOTA
   - 搜索可能遗漏的相关工作和 concurrent work

2. **深度阅读**：用 WebFetch 实际阅读找到的关键论文的 abstract 和方法部分，
   不要只依赖搜索摘要。形成你自己对领域现状的独立判断。

3. **深度思考**：在修订之前，先独立思考以下问题：
   - 这个 idea 的核心假设是否仍然成立？
   - reviewer 的批评是否揭示了更深层的问题？
   - 有没有更好的 framing 或 approach 来解决同一个核心问题？

SparseDM proposes a method based on the improved Straight-Through Estimator to improve deployment efficiency of diffusion models by adding sparse masks to Convolution and Linear layers in pre-trained models and fine-tuning them during the training stage. ## Being-H0.7: Latent World-Action Model

Being-H0.7 is a latent world-action model that brings future-aware reasoning into VLA-style policies without generating future frames. It inserts learnable latent queries between perception and action as a compact reasoning interface, and trains them with a future-informed dual-branch design: a deployable prior branch infers latent states from the current context, while a training-only posterior branch replaces the queries with embeddings from future observations.

### Architecture and Training

In the deployable prior branch, learnable latent queries are slotted to infer action-useful predictive factors from current multimodal context. In the posterior branch, these queries are replaced with embeddings extracted from subsequent observations, while the rest of the architecture remains unchanged. This branch provides an implicit training target: what information, if revealed by later observations, is useful for action prediction?

This design enables the model to efficiently realize the latent world-action modeling through the dual-branch formulation within a single backbone forward pass.

### Deployment and Training Data

At inference, the posterior branch is removed entirely: Being-H0.7 performs no future-frame generation or pixel-space rollout before acting. It preserves the efficiency of VLAs while injecting a world-modeling signal directly tied to action generation.

Being-H0.7 is trained on 200,000 hours of egocentric human videos together with 15,000 hours of robot demonstrations.

### Performance

Experiments across six simulation benchmarks and diverse real-world tasks show that Being-H0.7 achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance, combining the predictive benefits of world models with the efficiency and deployability of direct VLA policies.

## OA-WAM Overview

OA-WAM makes world-action modeling object-addressable through a slot-aware 7B trunk that routes cross-slot attention through a frozen per-object identity address.

## Performance on LIBERO-Plus (Geometric Axes)

On the LIBERO-Plus robustness benchmark, OA-WAM sets a new SOTA on the geometric axes most aligned with the hypothesis—camera achieving 85.7%, with the residual gap concentrated on Sensor Noise where photometric corruption disrupts slot extraction at the perception stage rather than the action policy itself.

## In-Distribution Performance

On in-distribution LIBERO and SimplerEnv WidowX (Visual Matching) it reaches 79.3% average success rate, leading all published VLA and WAM baselines.

## Architectural Innovation

Object addressability is enforced architecturally by routing cross-slot attention on the addr alone at every transformer layer—an addr-only key projection together with a per-layer reset of the addr slice in the residual stream, which separates "which object to act on" from "what that object currently is" at the tensor level.

## Limitations

Validation is simulator-only; reported robustness does not yet prove real-robot deployment.

## CKT-WAM Overview

CKT-WAM is a parameter-efficient Context Knowledge Transfer framework that transfers teacher WAM's knowledge into a student WAM through a compact context in the text embedding space, rather than output imitation or dense hidden-state matching.

## Technical Approach

CKT-WAM extracts intermediate teacher hidden states, reduces the number of tokens via compressors' learnable-query cross attention (LQCA), and transforms them through an always-on generalized adapter, a lightweight router, and sparsely activated specialized adapters. The resulting context is then appended to the student's conditioning textual embeddings, thereby injecting the transferred knowledge into the student with minimal architectural modification.

## LIBERO-Plus Results (2026)

CKT-WAM achieves the best overall performance on LIBERO-Plus, reaching 86.1% total success rate with only 1.17% trainable parameters, while approaching full fine-tuning performance. Beyond simulation, CKT-WAM also demonstrates strong real-world long-horizon manipulation ability, achieving the best average success rate of 83.3% across four multi-step tasks.

## CFG-DP Overview

CFG-DP is a novel framework to enhance Diffusion Policy by integrating Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) with conditional and unconditional models.

## Problem it Addresses

Temporal sequential tasks challenge humanoid robots, as existing Diffusion Policy (DP) and Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) methods often lack temporal context, resulting in local optima traps and excessive repetitive actions.

## How It Works

CFG leverages timestep inputs to track task progression and ensure precise cycle termination. It dynamically adjusts action predictions based on task phase, using a guidance factor tuned to balance temporal coherence and action accuracy.

## Experimental Results

Real-world experiments on a humanoid robot demonstrate high success rates and minimal repetitive actions. The paper was published in October 2025 and includes ablation studies examining different components and parameter adjustments affecting performance.

The research specifically focuses on robotic tasks like screw-tightening, where the robot needs to know when to stop repeating a cyclic action—a capability that previous diffusion policy methods struggled with due to their lack of temporal awareness.

## ADPro: Adaptive Diffusion Policy

ADPro is a test-time adaptation method that introduces two key inductive biases into diffusion: first, it embeds a geometric manifold constraint that aligns denoising updates with task-relevant subspaces, leveraging the relative pose between the end-effector and target scene to guide denoising along the geodesic path of the manipulation manifold. Second, it proposes an analytically guided initialization that computes a rough registration between the gripper and target scenes to propose a structured initial noisy action.

ADP is compatible with pre-trained diffusion policies and requires no retraining, enabling test-time adaptation that tailors the policy to specific tasks, thereby enhancing generalization across novel tasks and environments. Experiments on RLBench, CALVIN, and real-world datasets show that ADPro achieves up to 25% faster execution and 9% points improvement over strong diffusion baselines.

## Test-Time Perturbation Learning (TTPL) for VLAs

Perturbation learning with Delayed Feedback (PDF) is a verifier-free test-time adaptation framework that improves decision performance without fine-tuning the base model, mitigating spurious correlations through uncertainty-based data augmentation and action voting, while learning a lightweight perturbation module that retrospectively adjusts action logits guided by delayed feedback to correct overconfidence.

Experiments on LIBERO and Atari demonstrate consistent gains of PDF in task success over vanilla VLA, with improvements of +7.4% success rate on LIBERO and +10.3 human normalized score on Atari.

Both methods represent recent advances in test-time adaptation for robotic control systems, addressing the challenge of adapting pre-trained models to novel tasks and environments without requiring retraining.

## Video Branch Architecture for Spatial/Geometric Features

In world action models, **the video branch encodes spatial and geometric features** through multiple approaches:

### Dedicated Depth/Geometry Branches

Recent models like X-WAM use a dedicated depth branch created by replicating the final blocks of a pretrained Diffusion Transformer to achieve high-quality spatial modeling and reconstruction of future spatial information. The depth branch runs in an interleaved fashion with the main RGB branch, reading from the main branch via cross-attention but not affecting it, which preserves pretrained visual priors while enabling high-quality spatial reconstruction.

### Structured Kinematic-to-Visual Action Fields

Models like EA-WM render depth-aware arm structures, joint landmarks, gripper geometry, end-effector heatmaps, and pose cues as temporally aligned visual fields, bringing action conditioning into the same image domain as future video generation and providing richer spatial and geometric cues.

### Geometry-Aware Representations

Geometry-aware world model architectures structure the agent's internal representation of the environment using mathematical geometry and group actions, fundamentally altering inference and the ability to generalize spatial relationships.

These approaches address the critical limitation that 2D pixel-space observation models lack explicit spatial awareness and 3D geometric grounding, causing models to hallucinate physically implausible futures and preventing geometrically faithful 3D reconstruction.

## Independent Condition Guidance (ICG) Overview

Independent Condition Guidance (ICG) is a training-free solution that samples a random condition as negative instead of unconditional. The purpose of this approach is to provide a training-free alternative for conditional models that have not been trained with conditional dropout.

## Key Advantages

ICG provides the benefits of classifier-free guidance (CFG) without the need for any special training procedures. ICG and TSG (Time-Step Guidance) are easy to implement, do not require additional fine-tuning of the underlying diffusion models, and have the same sampling cost as CFG.

## Performance

ICG offers performance similar to CFG and can be readily applied to models that are not trained with the CFG objective in mind, such as EDM. ICG is able to achieve similar metrics to the standard CFG by extracting the unconditional score from the conditional model itself.

## Application to Robot Control

For sequential control, CFG-DP uses task progression (e.g., timestep input) to schedule guidance strength, enforcing temporal coherence, decisive action termination, and high success rates. Additionally, Decision Diffuser directly conditions the diffusion model on the return of the trajectory using classifier-free guidance and outperforms other approaches on a variety of tasks, such as block-stacking tasks.

## X-WAM: Unified 4D World Action Modeling

X-WAM is a unified 4D World Action Model that incorporates explicit 3D spatial awareness into the joint video-action modeling paradigm.

### Asynchronous Denoising with Independent Timesteps

X-WAM proposes Asynchronous Noise Sampling (ANS) to jointly optimize generation quality and action decoding efficiency, which applies a specialized asynchronous denoising schedule during inference that rapidly decodes actions with fewer steps to enable efficient real-time execution, while dedicating the full sequence of steps to generate high-fidelity video.

Rather than completely decoupling the noise timesteps of these modalities via independent random sampling, ANS systematically samples from a joint distribution of video and actions that strictly matches the test-time distribution, which elegantly eliminates the inefficiencies of decoupled sampling, maximizing both action inference speed and visual generation quality.

The research addresses the challenge of efficiently managing the different computational requirements of video and action modalities in unified world action models for robotic control.

## Overview

Motus is a unified latent action world model that leverages existing pretrained models and rich, sharable motion information.

## Architecture

Motus introduces a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture to integrate three experts (understanding, action, and video generation) and adopts a UniDiffuser-style scheduler to enable flexible switching between different modeling modes (World Models, Vision-Language-Action Models, Inverse Dynamics Models, Video Generation Models, and Video-Action Joint Prediction Models).

Motus further leverages optical flow to learn latent actions and adopts a three-phase training pipeline and six-layer data pyramid, thereby extracting pixel-level "delta action" and enabling large-scale action pretraining.

## Motus: A Unified Latent Action World Model

Motus is a unified latent action world model that leverages existing general pretrained models and rich, sharable motion information.

### Architecture and Cross-Modal Design

Motus introduces a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture to integrate three experts (understanding, video generation, and action) and adopts a UniDiffuser-style scheduler to enable flexible switching between different modeling modes (world models, vision-language-action models, inverse dynamics models, video generation models, and video-action joint prediction models).

The three experts include a Generative Expert (pre-trained video generation model), an Understanding Expert (pre-trained vision-language model), and an Action Expert, and they interact through shared multi-head self-attention layers, allowing for rich cross-modal fusion while letting each expert retain its specialized function.

### Timestep Marginalization and Scheduler

Motus incorporates a UniDiffuser-style scheduler to coordinate multimodal generation and allow flexible switching between different modeling modes, allocating distinct timesteps and noise scales to each modality (videos and actions), enabling the model to simultaneously learn marginal, conditional, and joint distributions.

### Training and Performance

Motus leverages optical flow to learn latent actions and adopts a recipe with three-phase training pipeline and six-layer data pyramid, thereby extracting pixel-level "delta action" and enabling large-scale action pretraining.

Experiments show that Motus achieves superior performance against state-of-the-art methods in both simulation (a +15% improvement over X-VLA and a +45% improvement over Pi0.5) and real-world scenarios (improved by +11~48%).

Based on the search results, here are the key details about the DiffStateGrad paper published at ICLR 2025:

## Paper Overview

The paper is titled "Diffusion State-Guided Projected Gradient for Inverse Problems" by Rayhan Zirvi, Bahareh Tolooshams, and Anima Anandkumar, published at The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations in 2025.

## Core Contribution

DiffStateGrad enhances diffusion-based inverse problem solvers by projecting measurement guidance gradients onto a data-driven low-rank subspace defined by intermediate diffusion states. More specifically, the projection is achieved by performing singular value decomposition (SVD) on the diffusion state of an image to which guidance is applied and using the highest contributing singular vectors as a projection matrix.

## Problem Addressed

For general inverse problems, approximations are needed when an unconditionally trained diffusion model is used since the measurement likelihood is intractable, leading to inaccurate posterior sampling. Due to these approximations, methods fail to preserve the generation process on the data manifold defined by the diffusion prior, leading to artifacts in applications such as image restoration.

## Key Advantages

DiffStateGrad can be added to a wide range of diffusion-based inverse solvers to improve preservation of the diffusion process on the prior manifold and filter out artifact-inducing components. It improves the robustness of diffusion models in terms of the choice of measurement guidance step size and noise while improving worst-case performance.

## Experimental Results

The most significant improvements appear in challenging tasks such as phase retrieval, HDR, and inpainting. By constraining solutions closer to the data manifold, DiffStateGrad minimizes extreme failures and enhances consistency in reconstruction quality.

## Paper Overview

The paper is titled "Diffusion State-Guided Projected Gradient for Inverse Problems" by Rayhan Zirvi, Bahareh Tolooshams, and Anima Anandkumar, published at The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations in 2025.

## Core Contribution

DiffStateGrad enhances diffusion-based inverse problem solvers by projecting measurement guidance gradients onto a data-driven low-rank subspace defined by intermediate diffusion states. More specifically, the projection is achieved by performing singular value decomposition (SVD) on the diffusion state of an image to which guidance is applied and using the highest contributing singular vectors as a projection matrix.

## Problem Addressed

For general inverse problems, approximations are needed when an unconditionally trained diffusion model is used since the measurement likelihood is intractable, leading to inaccurate posterior sampling. Due to these approximations, methods fail to preserve the generation process on the data manifold defined by the diffusion prior, leading to artifacts in applications such as image restoration.

## Key Advantages

DiffStateGrad can be added to a wide range of diffusion-based inverse solvers to improve preservation of the diffusion process on the prior manifold and filter out artifact-inducing components. It improves the robustness of diffusion models in terms of the choice of measurement guidance step size and noise while improving worst-case performance.

## Experimental Results

The most significant improvements appear in challenging tasks such as phase retrieval, HDR, and inpainting. By constraining solutions closer to the data manifold, DiffStateGrad minimizes extreme failures and enhances consistency in reconstruction quality.

Based on the search results, I found research on the "Compose Your Policies" paper. Here's what the research covers:

## Overview

"Compose Your Policies! Improving Diffusion-based or Flow-based Robot Policies via Test-time Distribution-level Composition" is a recent paper published in October 2025.

## Key Contribution

The work introduces an alternative paradigm for enhancing policy performance without additional model training, and demonstrates that the composed policies can exceed the performance of either parent policy.

## Technical Approach

The research establishes a theoretical foundation showing that the convex composition of distributional scores from multiple diffusion models can yield a superior one-step functional objective compared to any individual score, and a Grönwall-type bound is used to show that this single-step improvement propagates through entire generation trajectories, leading to systemic performance gains.

By combining distributional scores from pre-trained diffusion-based or flow-based policies on different conditions (e.g., visual modalities and network backbones), the method can generate expressive and adaptable action trajectories through convex score combination without additional training.

## Evaluation

The work evaluates on Robomimic (which includes three manipulation tasks: Can, Lift, Square), PushT, and RoboTwin (a suite of dual-arm collaborative tasks), and further performs four real-world experiments: Place Bottles, Hang Mug, Close Table, and Punch Holes.

I found comprehensive information about Modality-Composable Diffusion Policy (MCDP). Here are the key findings:

## Overview

Modality-Composable Diffusion Policy (MCDP) is a novel policy composition method that leverages multiple pre-trained diffusion policies (DPs) based on individual visual modalities, combining their distributional scores to form a more expressive policy without the need for additional training.

## Problem it Addresses

Current diffusion policies are often based on a single visual modality (e.g., RGB or point cloud), limiting their accuracy and generalization potential, and training a generalized DP capable of handling heterogeneous multimodal data would entail substantial computational and data-related costs.

## Key Advantages

Policies are trained independently on each modality using available data rather than a costly joint dataset, and these modular policies can then be flexibly recombined during deployment by adjusting the weighting coefficients without any new model retraining.

MCDP facilitates fusing information from multiple perception modalities without unified large-scale datasets, supports DPs trained on different robots or simulation domains to be composed, and enables rapid policy adaptation when new sensors become available.

## Empirical Results

When both constituent diffusion policies have moderate efficacy, composing them at inference consistently yields higher task success rates than either alone, with an example on the Empty Cup Place task showing success improved from 0.42 and 0.62 to 0.86 with optimal weighting.

The paper was published on arXiv in March 2025 and is associated with ICLR GenBot 2025, with code released on GitHub.

## Key findings from research:

### 1. UWM Fine-tuning Performance
- UWM achieves ~79% average on LIBERO after pretraining on LIBERO-90 and fine-tuning for 10K steps on 5 evaluation tasks
- This is pretraining + fine-tuning, NOT just pretraining. The 79% IS the fine-tuned result.
- This is a CRITICAL problem. The proposal claimed 79% was "pretraining-only" and fine-tuning would push it to >90%. 

But the UWM paper shows 79% is already the fine-tuned result, which means UWM is structurally weaker than the current state-of-the-art methods like Fast-WAM at 97.6% and Being-H0.7 at 99.2%.

### 2. LIBERO-Plus SOTA (Updated)
- OA-WAM: Camera 80.5%, Robot 89.6%, Geo-Avg 84.3%, Overall 83.9%
- π0.5: Overall 85.7%  
- CKT-WAM: Overall 86.1%
- Being-H0.7: 82.1% zero-shot, 84.8% fine-tuned
- Cosmos-Policy: 82.2%
- OA-WAM achieves 97.8% on standard LIBERO

### 3. Alternative backbones
Looking at other approaches: Motus uses independent timesteps like UniDiffuser but lacks clear CFG support, X-WAM explicitly couples modalities during training so it can't do independent timestep control, and MotuBrain shows 95.8% on RoboTwin though I haven't found LIBERO results for it.

### 4. Competing training-free methods
There are several other test-time adaptation approaches worth considering: AnyCamVLA handles camera adaptation through novel view synthesis, ADPro uses manifold constraints for adaptive diffusion policies on RLBench and CALVIN, and TTPL achieves a +7.4 improvement through test-time perturbation learning for VLAs.

### 5. Field trajectory and emerging patterns
I'm seeing methods like GPC that compose policies at test time without retraining, MCDP which does modality composition at inference time (this seems quite relevant), and CFG-DP applying classifier-free guidance to diffusion policies in temporal tasks. The broader field is actually diversifying rather than converging — Being-H0.7 uses implicit world modeling without explicit video branches, OA-WAM uses object-addressable architecture, and while the strongest methods are increasingly specialized, they're not all moving in the same direction away from video.

The core hypothesis also lacks empirical grounding — three independent works demonstrate that video is dispensable for these tasks, yet the proposal speculates that geometric perturbation changes this without any supporting evidence. Beyond that, the competitive landscape is more crowded than acknowledged: AnyCamVLA already handles training-free camera adaptation, ADPro provides training-free test-time adaptation for diffusion policies, and MCDP does training-free modality composition.   "approach": "We propose Spectral Cross-Modal Guidance (SCG), a training-free inference-time method for selectively amplifying action-relevant world knowledge in multi-modal diffusion policies. SCG spectrally decomposes the cross-modal guidance vector and retains only components whose Action Quality Correlation (AQC) indicates positive contribution to action quality. The approach is structured in three phases: backbone verification, cross-modal guidance diagnostics, and spectral filtering — with the method contribution (spectral decomposition + AQC selection) designed to provide value REGARDLESS of whether uniform CFG improves robustness.\n\n**Pre-Phase — Backbone Verification (Days 1-3, ~15h H100).** Before any SCG work, we resolve the UWM baseline uncertainty. UWM's published 79% average on LIBERO uses a harder evaluation protocol (unseen LIBERO-10 tasks, 10K fine-tuning steps from LIBERO-90 pretraining) than the standard suites (LIBERO-Spatial/Object/Goal/Long, 50 demos per task, trained to convergence). Step 1: Fine-tune UWM on 2 standard LIBERO suites (LIBERO-Long, LIBERO-Spatial) using the released fine-tuning code, training to convergence (~5h). Step 2: Evaluate on standard LIBERO (expect >88% if the pretraining provides effective initialization). Step 3: Evaluate on LIBERO-Plus camera and robot-init perturbations at L1 difficulty (~10h). Decision gate: If UWM achieves >88% on standard LIBERO suites, proceed with UWM. If 80-88%, proceed but note the baseline gap explicitly. If <80%, switch to Motus (UniDiffuser-style scheduler, stronger reported performance, checkpoint available). This 3-day investment eliminates the primary risk before committing to the full plan.\n\n**Phase 1 — Cross-Modal Guidance Diagnostics (~25-30h H100).** Using the verified backbone, we answer the foundational question: what is the NET effect of uniform cross-modal guidance under geometric perturbation? Using UWM's independent timestep mechanism, compute the guidance vector g_t = ε(a; t_a, t_o'=t_a) − ε(a; t_a, t_o'=T) at each action denoising step t. The guided prediction: ε_guided = ε_marginal + w·g_t. Sweep w ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0} on both standard LIBERO (sanity check) and LIBERO-Plus geometric perturbations (camera, robot-init at L1/L3 difficulty). INTERPRETATION PROTOCOL — three scenarios drive Phase 2 strategy: (A) Uniform CFG helps: SCG refines by filtering noise from the signal. (B) Uniform CFG is neutral/inconsistent: SCG decomposes the mixed-sign signal to extract positive components. (C) Uniform CFG hurts: SCG identifies and suppresses harmful components, potentially recovering buried positive signal. All three scenarios produce a method paper. Only if the guidance vector g_t is structurally pure noise (zero correlation between ANY component and action quality — verifiable via AQC analysis in Phase 2) does the paper reduce to a negative result. This is unlikely given that video-conditioned and video-marginalized predictions differ in encoding spatial information, not just random noise.\n\n**Phase 2 — Spectral Cross-Modal Guidance (method contribution, ~40-60h H100).** SCG applies spectral filtering to selectively amplify action-relevant guidance components. This is the primary method contribution and proceeds regardless of Phase 1 outcome. Step 1 — Spectral Decomposition: Collect guidance vectors {g_t} across a calibration set (~100 trajectories from STANDARD LIBERO training data, no perturbation needed) at each of K=10 denoising steps. For each step t, compute the SVD of the guidance covariance C_t = (1/N)Σ g_t g_t^T = U_t Λ_t U_t^T. Step 2 — Action Quality Correlation (AQC): For each principal direction u_i, compute the Spearman rank correlation between |u_i^T g_t| (projection magnitude) and action quality improvement (measured as reduction in L2 distance between predicted and ground-truth action). Retain components whose AQC exceeds a permutation-null threshold (p<0.05), yielding projection Π_t. This makes component selection automatic and parameter-free, based on empirical action-quality correlation rather than variance ranking. KEY DISTINCTION FROM CPC: AQC selects based on action-quality correlation, which is ORTHOGONAL to CPC's implicit variance-based selection. AQC may capture low-variance but high-quality-correlation components that CPC would suppress as 'negative CPCs,' and suppress high-variance components that CPC would amplify but that correspond to appearance variation rather than action-relevant geometry. Step 3 — Filtered Guidance: ε_guided = ε_marginal + w(t)·Π_t(g_t), where w(t) follows timestep-adaptive scheduling (β-CFG style). Step 4 — Sparse Guidance (efficiency contribution): The AQC decomposition reveals that only k << d guidance dimensions have significant action-quality correlation. This enables 'sparse guidance' — a low-rank approximation of the guidance signal using only the top-k AQC components. Sparse guidance reduces the effective dimensionality of the guidance computation, potentially enabling fewer denoising steps for equivalent quality. This efficiency contribution is independent of robustness improvement: even if SCG provides no robustness benefit, characterizing the effective dimensionality of cross-modal guidance and achieving equivalent quality with fewer dimensions is a standalone contribution applicable to any multi-modal diffusion model.\n\n**Calibration Transferability (explicit experimental plan).** A key practical question is whether the AQC-selected subspace is stable or requires per-task recalibration. We address this with systematic ablations: (a) Cross-task transfer: calibrate AQC on LIBERO tasks A, evaluate on tasks B — if the action-relevant subspace is a property of the model architecture rather than task specifics, transfer should be high. (b) Cross-perturbation transfer: calibrate on standard (unperturbed) data, evaluate on camera and robot-init perturbations — the hypothesis is that action-relevant guidance dimensions are perturbation-invariant because they encode geometric structure, not perturbation-specific appearance. (c) Cross-difficulty transfer: calibrate at L1, evaluate at L3. If transfer holds, SCG requires only one-time calibration per model — making it genuinely training-free. If partial transfer, SCG still requires orders-of-magnitude less data than OA-WAM (architectural modification) or CKT-WAM (parameter-efficient training with full training pipeline).\n\n**Backbone Strategy.** Primary: UWM with LIBERO-90 checkpoint, verified via Pre-Phase. UWM's independent timesteps provide mathematically clean cross-modal CFG. Secondary backbone (single-paragraph extension, not core): If time permits, apply ICG (Independent Condition Guidance, ICLR 2025) to Fast-WAM to test SCG's backbone-agnosticism. ICG approximates the unconditional score by conditioning on random/independent inputs — for Fast-WAM, substituting real video tokens with random embeddings sampled from a matched distribution. This tests whether SCG transfers across different CFG mechanisms (native independent timesteps vs. ICG approximation) and different backbone strengths (UWM vs. Fast-WAM 97.6%). This extension is scoped as a single experiment, not a core contribution.\n\n**Evaluation strategy.** Primary benchmark: LIBERO-Plus with geometric perturbation types (camera and robot-init, where spatial reasoning matters most), plus light as control (where WAMs already excel, expect no SCG benefit). 2 difficulty levels (L1, L3), 2 seeds. Standard LIBERO as sanity check. Baselines: (i) UWM standard policy (t_o'=T, no guidance), (ii) UWM joint denoising (t_o'=t_a, standard — equivalent to w=1.0), (iii) Uniform cross-modal CFG (w=1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0), (iv) SCG with AQC spectral filtering (ours), (v) SCG-Sparse (top-k AQC components only). Ablations: (a) AQC threshold sensitivity, (b) per-step vs. global SVD, (c) cross-task transfer of calibrated subspace, (d) cross-perturbation transfer (calibrate on standard, evaluate on perturbed), (e) AQC-selected vs. top-variance directions (testing whether action-relevant ≠ high-variance, validating the CPC-insufficiency argument), (f) sparse guidance dimensionality sweep (k = 5, 10, 20, 50, full). Framing vs. competitors: SCG is training-free and architecture-agnostic, complementary to OA-WAM (architectural) and CKT-WAM (training-based). Unlike AnyCamVLA (camera-only, VLA-specific) and MCDP (requires separate per-modality models), SCG works within a single multi-modal model and addresses both camera and robot-init perturbations. We position SCG as applicable to any WAM with distinguishable modality channels.",

## Summary of Changes (Major Revision)

Here's how each reviewer issue is addressed:

**Issue 1 (UWM BASE MODEL WEAKNESS — CRITICAL):** Corrected the false claim that 79% is pretraining-only. The 79% IS the fine-tuned result, but on a harder evaluation protocol (unseen LIBERO-10 tasks, 10K fine-tune steps) — not the standard LIBERO suites other methods report on. Added a Pre-Phase (Days 1-3) to verify UWM on standard LIBERO suites before committing. Added Motus as a fallback backbone with explicit decision thresholds.

**Issue 2 (NO LIBERO-PLUS BASELINE):** Pre-Phase now includes LIBERO-Plus L1 evaluation for the chosen backbone. This 3-day investment answers whether the backbone is competitive before committing 2+ weeks.

**Issue 3 (CONTINGENT METHOD CONTRIBUTION):** The core structural fix. SCG's method contribution is now Phase-1-independent via three-scenario analysis: uniform CFG helps → SCG refines; neutral → SCG separates mixed-sign components; hurts → SCG suppresses harmful components. Added sparse guidance as a standalone efficiency contribution. Only the extreme case of pure-noise guidance (zero AQC for all components) produces a null result.

**Issue 4 (NULL RESULT PROBABILITY):** Substantially reduced by the Phase-1-independent design. The method contribution exists in all scenarios except pure-noise guidance. The sparse guidance efficiency contribution is entirely independent of robustness outcomes.

**Issue 5 (CALIBRATION TRANSFERABILITY):** Now addressed with explicit experimental plan: cross-task transfer, cross-perturbation transfer (calibrate on standard data, evaluate on perturbed), and cross-difficulty transfer. Even worst-case (per-task calibration with 100 trajectories) is far cheaper than OA-WAM/CKT-WAM.

**Issue 6 (FIELD TRAJECTORY):** Acknowledged Being-H0.7's implicit approach. Argued SCG applies to any model with distinguishable modality channels. Noted explicit-branch WAMs remain dominant as of May 2026. Positioned SCG as a general principle, not tied to a specific architecture family.

**Reviewer Suggestion 4 (CPC DIFFERENTIATION):** Sharpened argument: CPC assumes class-conditional distributions with shared covariance (classes differ in means, not covariance structure). Video→action conditioning has structurally different conditional/unconditional covariances (different information levels, not different labels). AQC selects on action-quality correlation, orthogonal to CPC's variance-based implicit selection.

**Reviewer Suggestion 5 (ICG SCOPED):** ICG-on-Fast-WAM now explicitly scoped as single-paragraph extension, not core contribution.

**New additions:** MCDP and GPC-Composition added to landscape with clear differentiation (separate-model uniform composition vs. single-model spectral selective amplification). Updated all LIBERO-Plus numbers with verified data from the robustness study. X-WAM corrected (couples modalities, does NOT support cross-modal CFG).
